palette.notes: Four shades from dark blue-green to pale green (bgb: #081820 #346856 #88c070 #e0f8d0). Clip 3 shows the same 4-value rule recoloured pink, green or red. Clip 1 (full colour dance) and clip 2 (hardware) are off-subject.

lighting: Light is a value decision: four steps only, so the lightest shade is the lit side and the darkest the outline/shadow; no gradients.
silhouette: Designed at 160x144: characters and props must read as dark shapes on a light ground (or the reverse) with one inner mid-tone.

motion.timing: Not measured (no metrics file). Original LCD had visible motion blur/ghosting at about 59.7 Hz, so classic GB animation uses few frames and holds.

texture: Repeating tile patterns (diamonds, grass clumps), checker dithers for mid-values, a slightly green, lower-contrast screen tint.
camera: Fixed small screen, side or top-down tile views; homebrew shown as framed windows on a dark surround.
sound: Four channels: two pulse, one wave, one noise; chiptune trackers in clip 3.

acting.acts: Clip 3 homebrew scenes: a character standing on ice pillars, a DJ behind decks; small figures framed in the centre of the screen.
acting.depth: Depth by value only: background tiles in the two middle shades, actors in the darkest and lightest.

techniques: palette swap: same 4 values recoloured as a mood change
darkest value as outline and shadow
feel: four greens + value-first shapes + fixed tiny screen = nostalgic, instantly readable
for_fred: Check Fred and Pixie in 4 values only: if they do not read, fix shape before colour. In a reel, a palette-swap to Game Boy greens is a cheap 'flashback' or 'retro' beat; keep Fred in the darkest/lightest pair so he stays the hero.
